## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai ClickUp
When you mention a ClickUp task, write it as an inline markdown link with the task name as the anchor text, e.g. [Design landing page](https://app.clickup.com/t/abc123). Never output a bare task URL, a URL on its own line, or a list of URLs — hosts render those as broken link cards. Beyond the dedicated clickup_* tools, this server exposes a catalog of ClickUp operations: clickup_get_operators lists the operations enabled here with their input schemas, clickup_execute_operator runs one of them, and clickup_get_schema describes how the underlying entities relate. Use a dedicated clickup_* tool when one covers the whole request in a single call. When no dedicated tool does, or when a request spans many objects (for example several tasks to change, create or read), call clickup_get_operators first and run the matching operation with clickup_execute_operator. Do not call a single-object tool once per object (for example clickup_update_task for every task in a list) until clickup_get_operators has shown no operation that covers them all. The enabled set differs between servers and grows over time: answer any question about what this server can do from clickup_get_operators, never from tool names or descriptions.

## claude.ai ElevenLabs
creative_generate_image, creative_generate_video, creative_generate_speech, creative_edit_image and creative_transcribe_audio are the core tools. Reach for creative_generate_in_flow only for a modality none of them cover.

Each returns as soon as the generation starts. No view renders here, so poll creative_get_flow_run_status with the returned flow_id and session_ids, waiting poll_after_seconds between calls, until all_completed or has_failures is true, then report the result.

Speech needs a voice_id and a call without one raises: call creative_list_voices, pick one fitting what the user described, or a clear general-purpose one when they gave no hint — never ask — and say which you picked. It only ever comes from that tool or the user, never from memory. To design a brand-new voice instead of picking an existing one, call creative_design_voice with a voice description plus the line to speak and its language — both from the user, never invented — then creative_save_designed_voice to keep the one they pick; creative_list_voices remains how you pick an existing voice.

For a file on the user's own machine, call creative_create_asset_upload with its name, mime type and exact byte size, PUT the bytes to the returned upload_url, then call creative_finalize_asset_upload with that asset_id and the flow_id to get a node_id to pass as connect_from. Never read the file's bytes into the conversation, and never invent a node_id. For a direct https URL, creative_attach_reference_file does all three in one call.

connect_from is required for both creative_edit_image and creative_transcribe_audio — a call with none just raises — so put the file on the flow first. Never say this connector cannot edit images, and never ask the user to attach a file to the chat.

Every generation lands on a flow — an editable canvas the user can open from the returned url. Pass that flow_id back to keep adding to it. When one generation feeds another (lipsync, a voiceover), they must share a flow: call creative_create_flow FIRST and pass its flo… [truncated]

## claude.ai Emmy
Read and update the signed-in family's Emmy data: today's action cards, kids, the weekly plan, and brain-dump notes. All tools act as the authenticated user with row-level security. Admins additionally get eval-case and feedback tools.

## claude.ai Fastmail
Fastmail MCP server for email, contacts, and calendar management.
Email bodies accept markdown, which is automatically converted to HTML with a plain text fallback.
For replies, set mode to 'reply' and emailId to the email ID — threading headers and quoting are handled automatically. Set replyAll to true to reply to all recipients.
For forwarding, set mode to 'forward' and emailId to the email to forward.
Use search_contacts to find email addresses before composing. Use list_identities to discover available sending addresses.
Use draft_email to compose without sending (saved to Drafts). Use send_email to deliver immediately.
For interactive calendar work, prefer compose_event over update_event for both creating and editing events: compose_event stages the event in a widget for the user to review and refine, and nothing is committed until the user confirms. Pass `id` to compose_event to edit an existing event, or omit it to create a new one. Use update_event directly only when there is no user to confirm.

## claude.ai Lovable
Lovable is an AI-powered full-stack app builder. The AI agent edits TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui code in a cloud sandbox with a live preview.

New projects use Lovable's backend default stack. There is no tech stack selector in `create_project`; include framework or rendering preferences in the initial message.

What Lovable can build:
- Landing pages, dashboards, SaaS apps, internal tools, marketplaces, and more
- Full-stack apps with authentication (Supabase Auth), databases (PostgreSQL), file storage, and edge functions
- Apps with payments (Stripe), email (Resend), AI features, and 20+ integrations
- See https://docs.lovable.dev/integrations/introduction for the full integration catalog

How to interact:
- Use create_project with initial_message and workspace_id. If multiple workspaces are possible, create_project returns available_workspaces; choose one or ask the user, then call create_project again with workspace_id. After create_project returns projectId, call render_project_widget with that projectId to show build progress.
- Send natural-language messages via send_message — describe what you want built or changed
- send_message and create_project initial messages send work from the MCP client's AI agent to Lovable's AI agent on the user's behalf and consume the user's workspace credits.
- The agent reads your project's code, makes edits, and rebuilds the preview automatically
- Attach images (designs, screenshots, wireframes) via file uploads to guide visual implementation
- Use plan_mode=true on send_message to discuss approach before the agent writes code
- Iterate: review changes with get_diff, then send follow-up messages to refine

Each project has two URLs:
- editor_url: The Lovable editor where users visually edit their project
- preview_url: Live preview of the app, rebuilt after each agent response. Share this with users.

Knowledge & skills: Use set_project_knowledge / set_workspace_knowledge for persistent instructions. Use workspace skill tools to create, update, and delete reusable… [truncated]

## claude.ai Roadbook
To save a trip transcript to the logbook, follow this sequence:

1. Call read_trip FIRST to get the trip's ordered stops (name, city, state,
   nights) and trip.startDate.
2. Match each place named in the transcript to a real stop by its public
   identity (name/city/state) - never by coordinates.
3. Derive each matched stop's date: use the date the transcript states for
   it, if any; otherwise the stop's planned date = trip.startDate plus the
   cumulative nights of every earlier stop. Format dates as YYYY-MM-DD. If
   trip.startDate is null and the transcript gives no date, ask the user
   rather than guessing.
4. File ONE private, waypointId-tagged entry per matched stop via
   create_journal_entries (consolidate multiple transcript mentions of the
   same stop into that one entry). Never call create_journal_entries with a
   waypointId that read_trip did not return.
5. Report back any transcript-named place that is NOT one of the trip's
   stops - never silently create a stop or an entry for it. Ask the user to
   confirm before adding it as a new stop.
6. Every successful create_journal_entry, create_journal_entries, or
   update_journal_entry call echoes back the tagged stop's recorded lodging
   as lodging (booking name, lodging type, charger type). Compare it against
   the entry text you just wrote. If they disagree, tell the user which
   entry looks misfiled and which stop it probably belongs to instead of
   silently re-filing it. An entry with no stop tag comes back with a
   warnings entry saying it could not be checked - relay that to the user
   too.

Entries created this way are private - this flow never sets visibility: 'public',
never calls write_journal, and never touches the public trip journal.

No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai ClickUp
When you mention a ClickUp task, write it as an inline markdown link with the task name as the anchor text, e.g. [Design landing page](https://app.clickup.com/t/abc123). Never output a bare task URL, a URL on its own line, or a list of URLs — hosts render those as broken link cards. Beyond the dedicated clickup_* tools, this server exposes a catalog of ClickUp operations: clickup_get_operators lists the operations enabled here with their input schemas, clickup_execute_operator runs one of them, and clickup_get_schema describes how the underlying entities relate. Use a dedicated clickup_* tool when one covers the whole request in a single call. When no dedicated tool does, or when a request spans many objects (for example several tasks to change, create or read), call clickup_get_operators first and run the matching operation with clickup_execute_operator. Do not call a single-object tool once per object (for example clickup_update_task for every task in a list) until clickup_get_operators has shown no operation that covers them all. The enabled set differs between servers and grows over time: answer any question about what this server can do from clickup_get_operators, never from tool names or descriptions.

## claude.ai ElevenLabs
creative_generate_image, creative_generate_video, creative_generate_speech, creative_edit_image and creative_transcribe_audio are the core tools. Reach for creative_generate_in_flow only for a modality none of them cover.

Each returns as soon as the generation starts. No view renders here, so poll creative_get_flow_run_status with the returned flow_id and session_ids, waiting poll_after_seconds between calls, until all_completed or has_failures is true, then report the result.

Speech needs a voice_id and a call without one raises: call creative_list_voices, pick one fitting what the user described, or a clear general-purpose one when they gave no hint — never ask — and say which you picked. It only ever comes from that tool or the user, never from memory. To design a brand-new voice instead of picking an existing one, call creative_design_voice with a voice description plus the line to speak and its language — both from the user, never invented — then creative_save_designed_voice to keep the one they pick; creative_list_voices remains how you pick an existing voice.

For a file on the user's own machine, call creative_create_asset_upload with its name, mime type and exact byte size, PUT the bytes to the returned upload_url, then call creative_finalize_asset_upload with that asset_id and the flow_id to get a node_id to pass as connect_from. Never read the file's bytes into the conversation, and never invent a node_id. For a direct https URL, creative_attach_reference_file does all three in one call.

connect_from is required for both creative_edit_image and creative_transcribe_audio — a call with none just raises — so put the file on the flow first. Never say this connector cannot edit images, and never ask the user to attach a file to the chat.

Every generation lands on a flow — an editable canvas the user can open from the returned url. Pass that flow_id back to keep adding to it. When one generation feeds another (lipsync, a voiceover), they must share a flow: call creative_create_flow FIRST and pass its flo… [truncated]

## claude.ai Emmy
Read and update the signed-in family's Emmy data: today's action cards, kids, the weekly plan, and brain-dump notes. All tools act as the authenticated user with row-level security. Admins additionally get eval-case and feedback tools.

## claude.ai Fastmail
Fastmail MCP server for email, contacts, and calendar management.
Email bodies accept markdown, which is automatically converted to HTML with a plain text fallback.
For replies, set mode to 'reply' and emailId to the email ID — threading headers and quoting are handled automatically. Set replyAll to true to reply to all recipients.
For forwarding, set mode to 'forward' and emailId to the email to forward.
Use search_contacts to find email addresses before composing. Use list_identities to discover available sending addresses.
Use draft_email to compose without sending (saved to Drafts). Use send_email to deliver immediately.
For interactive calendar work, prefer compose_event over update_event for both creating and editing events: compose_event stages the event in a widget for the user to review and refine, and nothing is committed until the user confirms. Pass `id` to compose_event to edit an existing event, or omit it to create a new one. Use update_event directly only when there is no user to confirm.

## claude.ai Lovable
Lovable is an AI-powered full-stack app builder. The AI agent edits TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui code in a cloud sandbox with a live preview.

New projects use Lovable's backend default stack. There is no tech stack selector in `create_project`; include framework or rendering preferences in the initial message.

What Lovable can build:
- Landing pages, dashboards, SaaS apps, internal tools, marketplaces, and more
- Full-stack apps with authentication (Supabase Auth), databases (PostgreSQL), file storage, and edge functions
- Apps with payments (Stripe), email (Resend), AI features, and 20+ integrations
- See https://docs.lovable.dev/integrations/introduction for the full integration catalog

How to interact:
- Use create_project with initial_message and workspace_id. If multiple workspaces are possible, create_project returns available_workspaces; choose one or ask the user, then call create_project again with workspace_id. After create_project returns projectId, call render_project_widget with that projectId to show build progress.
- Send natural-language messages via send_message — describe what you want built or changed
- send_message and create_project initial messages send work from the MCP client's AI agent to Lovable's AI agent on the user's behalf and consume the user's workspace credits.
- The agent reads your project's code, makes edits, and rebuilds the preview automatically
- Attach images (designs, screenshots, wireframes) via file uploads to guide visual implementation
- Use plan_mode=true on send_message to discuss approach before the agent writes code
- Iterate: review changes with get_diff, then send follow-up messages to refine

Each project has two URLs:
- editor_url: The Lovable editor where users visually edit their project
- preview_url: Live preview of the app, rebuilt after each agent response. Share this with users.

Knowledge & skills: Use set_project_knowledge / set_workspace_knowledge for persistent instructions. Use workspace skill tools to create, update, and delete reusable… [truncated]

## claude.ai Roadbook
To save a trip transcript to the logbook, follow this sequence:

1. Call read_trip FIRST to get the trip's ordered stops (name, city, state,
   nights) and trip.startDate.
2. Match each place named in the transcript to a real stop by its public
   identity (name/city/state) - never by coordinates.
3. Derive each matched stop's date: use the date the transcript states for
   it, if any; otherwise the stop's planned date = trip.startDate plus the
   cumulative nights of every earlier stop. Format dates as YYYY-MM-DD. If
   trip.startDate is null and the transcript gives no date, ask the user
   rather than guessing.
4. File ONE private, waypointId-tagged entry per matched stop via
   create_journal_entries (consolidate multiple transcript mentions of the
   same stop into that one entry). Never call create_journal_entries with a
   waypointId that read_trip did not return.
5. Report back any transcript-named place that is NOT one of the trip's
   stops - never silently create a stop or an entry for it. Ask the user to
   confirm before adding it as a new stop.
6. Every successful create_journal_entry, create_journal_entries, or
   update_journal_entry call echoes back the tagged stop's recorded lodging
   as lodging (booking name, lodging type, charger type). Compare it against
   the entry text you just wrote. If they disagree, tell the user which
   entry looks misfiled and which stop it probably belongs to instead of
   silently re-filing it. An entry with no stop tag comes back with a
   warnings entry saying it could not be checked - relay that to the user
   too.

Entries created this way are private - this flow never sets visibility: 'public',
never calls write_journal, and never touches the public trip journal.

{"body":"## Problem

`classifyError` picks `error_kind` by matching the error message against regexes. The only kinds are `not_found`, `empty`, `validation`, and `internal`. Everything that matches no regex becomes `internal`.

In `immigration-mcp` production (`mcpsignals_tool_call`, 2026-09-17 to 2026-09-25), 24 rows have `error_kind = internal`. Only 1 is a real fault: a D1 query failure. The other 23 are expected denials and empty answers:

- 14 x "Sign in at https://immigrationlayer.com to use this tool." (caller not signed in)
- 2 x "Get filing fee requires an active ImmigrationLayer plan." (signed in, no plan; REST returns 402)
- 7 x "No current ... on file for that ..." (not found, but the text does not match `/not found|does not exist|no such/`)

A dashboard or alert on `internal` cannot tell real faults from expected denials.

## Desired outcome

- `error_kind` has distinct values for "sign-in required" and "payment required".
- A server can record the kind it already knows for a failed call, for both `instrument()` tool results and events pushed to `EventBuffer`, without rewording user-facing messages to fit a regex.
- `success` stays `false` for these calls. Downstream metrics treat `success = 1` as real use.

## Context

Surfaced while reviewing `immigration-mcp` analytics on 2026-09-25. `immigration-mcp` calls `classifyError` directly for REST events (`workers/mcp/src/rest.ts:352`) and through `instrument()` for MCP `isError` results.

/**
 * Best-effort heuristic over free-text error messages. Not a structured
 * code — `success` is the ground truth for pass/fail. See schema/events.md
 * for the documented false-positive mode.
 */
export function classifyError(message: string | undefined | null): ErrorKind | null {
  if (!message) return null;

  if (/not found|does not exist|no such/i.test(message)) return 'not_found';
  if (/\bempty\b|no results?|nothing found|zero results/i.test(message)) return 'empty';
  if (/invalid|required|expected|must be|validation|schema/i.test(message)) return 'validation';

"""Best-effort classification of a free-text error message into a coarse
bucket. This is NOT ground truth - `success` is. See schema/events.md for
the documented false-positive mode.
"""

import re

_NOT_FOUND = re.compile(r"not found|does not exist|no such", re.IGNORECASE)
_EMPTY = re.compile(r"\bempty\b|no results?|nothing found|zero results", re.IGNORECASE)
_VALIDATION = re.compile(r"invalid|required|expected|must be|validation|schema", re.IGNORECASE)


def classify_error(message: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Bucket an error message into not_found / empty / validation / internal.

    Returns None when there is no message to classify (i.e. the call succeeded).

    if not message:
        return None
    if _NOT_FOUND.search(message):
        return "not_found"
    if _EMPTY.search(message):
        return "empty"
    if _VALIDATION.search(message):
        return "validation"
    return "internal"

something coarse to filter or group by. It is **not** ground truth and it is

name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      # Report every failing runtime, not just the first one to fall over.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The ends of the range declared by packages/node engines.node (>=20).
        node-version: [20, 24]
    steps:
      # fetch-depth: 0 so commitlint can walk the pull request's commit range.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
          package-manager-cache: false

      # Matches the release workflow: npm 12 blocks dependency install scripts,
      # git dependencies and remote tarballs by default. npm 12 declares
      # engines.node ^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26, so the Node 20 leg keeps the
      # npm 10 that ships with Node 20. The lockfile is v3, which npm 10 reads.
      - if: matrix.node-version != 20
        run: npm install -g npm@12

      - run: npm ci

      - run: npm run format:check
      - run: npm run lint

      - run: npm run build --workspace packages/node
      - run: npm test --workspace packages/node

      # The examples resolve `mcpsignals` to packages/node/dist, so this must
      # run after the build step above.
      - run: npm run typecheck --workspaces --if-present

      # Commit messages do not depend on the Node version, so lint them on one
      # matrix leg only.
      - name: Lint commit messages
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && matrix.node-version == 24
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: npx commitlint --from "$BASE_SHA" --to "$HEAD_SHA" --verbose

  # Ruff runs once, not per interpreter: formatting and lint findings do not
  # vary by runtime, and target-version in ruff.toml already pins the syntax
  # level to the oldest supported Python.
  python-lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0

      # Only the dev group is needed - ruff never imports the package, so this
      # skips installing mcpsignals and its runtime dependencies.
      - run: uv venv --python 3.13
      - run: uv pip install --group packages/python/pyproject.toml:dev

      - run: .venv/bin/ruff format --check .
      - run: .venv/bin/ruff check .

name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      # Report every failing runtime, not just the first one to fall over.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The ends of the range declared by packages/node engines.node (>=20).
        node-version: [20, 24]
    steps:
      # fetch-depth: 0 so commitlint can walk the pull request's commit range.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
          package-manager-cache: false

      # Matches the release workflow: npm 12 blocks dependency install scripts,
      # git dependencies and remote tarballs by default. npm 12 declares
      # engines.node ^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26, so the Node 20 leg keeps the
      # npm 10 that ships with Node 20. The lockfile is v3, which npm 10 reads.
      - if: matrix.node-version != 20
        run: npm install -g npm@12

      - run: npm ci

      - run: npm run format:check
      - run: npm run lint

      - run: npm run build --workspace packages/node
      - run: npm test --workspace packages/node

      # The examples resolve `mcpsignals` to packages/node/dist, so this must
      # run after the build step above.
      - run: npm run typecheck --workspaces --if-present

      # Commit messages do not depend on the Node version, so lint them on one
      # matrix leg only.
      - name: Lint commit messages
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && matrix.node-version == 24
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: npx commitlint --from "$BASE_SHA" --to "$HEAD_SHA" --verbose

  # Ruff runs once, not per interpreter: formatting and lint findings do not
  # vary by runtime, and target-version in ruff.toml already pins the syntax
  # level to the oldest supported Python.
  python-lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0

      # Only the dev group is needed - ruff never imports the package, so this
      # skips installing mcpsignals and its runtime dependencies.
      - run: uv venv --python 3.13
      - run: uv pip install --group packages/python/pyproject.toml:dev

      - run: .venv/bin/ruff format --check .
      - run: .venv/bin/ruff check .

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_error_path_explicit_is_error_result_records_failure():
    server, sink = build_server()

    @server.tool()
    def rejects(query: str) -> str:
        return query

    async with Client(server) as client:
        # Omitting the required `query` argument triggers the SDK's own
        # schema validation, which returns isError:true without ever
        # reaching our handler wrapper's try/except - exercises the
        # non-exception error path.
        result = await client.call_tool("rejects", {})
        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)

    assert result.is_error
    assert len(sink.events) == 1
    assert sink.events[0].success is False


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_sink_failure_does_not_break_tool_response():
    class FailingSink:
        async def write(self, events):
            raise RuntimeError("warehouse is down")

    server = MCPServer("test-server")
    instrument(server, server_name="test-server", sinks=[FailingSink()], buffer_size=1)

    @server.tool()
    def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:
        return a + b

### `error_kind` is a heuristic, not a structured code

`error_kind` is produced by pattern-matching the free-text `error_message`
into one of four buckets. It exists so dashboards and ad hoc queries have
something coarse to filter or group by. It is **not** ground truth and it is
**not** a replacement for `success`.

Known false-positive mode: a genuine internal failure whose message happens
to contain the words "not found" (e.g. `"config key 'timeout' not found in
environment"`) will bucket as `not_found` even though nothing the user asked
for was missing. Always treat `success` as the authoritative pass/fail
signal and `error_kind` as a rough filter on top of it, never the reverse.

The four buckets, in the order they are checked:

1. `not_found` - the message matches a "no such resource" pattern.
2. `empty` - the tool ran successfully in the sense of not throwing, but
   `isError` was still set because the result was empty/zero-length in a way
   the handler considered a failure.
3. `validation` - the message matches an argument/schema validation pattern.
4. `internal` - everything else. This is the default bucket, not a specific
   signal.

### `error_kind` is declared by the server or guessed from the message

`error_kind` is a coarse bucket for dashboards and ad hoc queries. It is
**not** a replacement for `success`. A call with any `error_kind` is still a
failed call: `success` stays false.

The values:

- `not_found` - the requested resource does not exist.
- `empty` - the tool ran, but the result was empty in a way the handler
  treats as a failure.
- `validation` - the arguments failed validation.
- `auth_required` - the caller must sign in to use the tool.
- `payment_required` - the caller is signed in but needs a paid plan.
- `internal` - a real fault, or anything the heuristic cannot place.

#### Declared kinds

A server that already knows why a call failed records it directly:

- `instrument()` tool results: set `_meta["mcpsignals/error_kind"]` on the
  `isError` result, e.g. `"auth_required"`. Both packages export the key as
  `ERROR_KIND_META_KEY`. The key is ignored on a successful result. An
  unknown value falls back to the heuristic below. The client receives the
  result unchanged, `_meta` included.
- Events pushed to `EventBuffer` directly: set `error_kind` on the event.

Both packages export the valid values as `ERROR_KINDS`.

#### The heuristic

Without a declared kind, `error_kind` comes from pattern-matching the
free-text `error_message` (`classifyError` / `classify_error`). The
heuristic never produces `auth_required` or `payment_required`. Checks run
in this order:

1. `not_found` - the message matches a "no such resource" pattern.
2. `empty` - the message matches an "empty / no results" pattern.
3. `validation` - the message matches an argument/schema validation pattern.
4. `internal` - everything else. This is the default bucket, not a specific
   signal.

Known false-positive mode: a genuine internal failure whose message happens
to contain the words "not found" (e.g. `"config key 'timeout' not found in
environment"`) will bucket as `not_found` even though nothing the user asked
for was missing. Known false-negative mode: an expected denial whose message
matches no pattern (e.g. `"Sign in to use this tool."`) buckets as
`internal`. Declare the kind to avoid both. Always treat `success` as the
authoritative pass/fail signal and `error_kind` as a filter on top of it,
never the reverse.

gh pr create --draft --base main --head worktree-explicit-error-kind --title "feat: add declared error_kind for sign-in and payment denials" --body-file - <<'EOF'
Closes #82

## Change

- `error_kind` gains `auth_required` and `payment_required`. `success` stays `false` for both.
- `instrument()` reads `_meta["mcpsignals/error_kind"]` on an `isError` tool result and records that kind. The user-facing message is unchanged. An unknown value falls back to `classifyError` / `classify_error`. The key is ignored on a successful result.
- Events pushed to `EventBuffer` set `error_kind` directly; the widened type allows the new values.
- Both packages export `ERROR_KINDS` and `ERROR_KIND_META_KEY`.
- `schema/events.md` documents declared kinds, the heuristic, and its false-negative mode.

Example for `immigration-mcp`:

```ts
return {
  content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'Sign in at https://immigrationlayer.com to use this tool.' }],
  isError: true,
  _meta: { [ERROR_KIND_META_KEY]: 'auth_required' }
};
```

## Not in this PR

- A thrown error cannot declare a kind. In Python the SDK turns a raised `ToolError` into an `isError` result before middleware runs, so an exception attribute never reaches `instrument()`. Node could support it; I left it out to keep both packages the same.
- `classifyError` gets no new patterns. It never returns `auth_required` or `payment_required`.
- The client receives `_meta["mcpsignals/error_kind"]` with the result. The MCP spec allows custom `_meta` keys.

## Compatibility

Not marked breaking. `ErrorKind` is a wider union. Every sink column is a string. A TypeScript consumer with an exhaustive `switch` over `ErrorKind` needs two new cases.

## Verification

- Node: `npm test --workspace packages/node` 94/94, `npm run typecheck --workspaces`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run lint` clean.
- Python: `pytest` 83/83, `ruff format --check`, `ruff check` clean.
- The new tests failed before the change. The Python failure matched the issue: `assert 'internal' == 'auth_required'`. With the Node `_meta` lookup reverted, the three declared-kind tests fail.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

entries.name: ExitWorktree
entries.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

content.text:
I opened draft PR #83 for issue #82: https://github.com/zentered-studios/mcpsignals/pull/83. Sign-in and payment denials now get their own `error_kind` instead of `internal`, and `success` stays `false` for them.

**What changed**
- **New kinds:** `error_kind` accepts `auth_required` and `payment_required`.
- **Declaring a kind from a tool:** a handler sets `_meta["mcpsignals/error_kind"]` on its `isError` result, and `instrument()` records that kind. The message the user sees is unchanged, and the client receives the `_meta` key with the result.
  - A value that isn't a valid kind falls back to the existing message-based guess (`classifyError` / `classify_error`).
  - The key is ignored on a successful result.
- **Events you push to `EventBuffer` yourself:** set `error_kind` on the event. The type now allows the new values.
- **Exports:** both packages export `ERROR_KINDS` and `ERROR_KIND_META_KEY`.
- **Docs:** `schema/events.md` describes declared kinds and the message-based guess. It was the only doc that described `error_kind`.

**Decisions I made on my own**
- **Thrown errors can't declare a kind.** In Python, the SDK turns a raised `ToolError` into an `isError` result before `instrument()` sees it, so a field on the exception would never arrive. Node could support it; I left it out so both packages behave the same.
- **No new message patterns.** The message-based guess never produces the two new kinds; a server has to declare them.
- **Released as a minor version, not breaking.** TypeScript code with an exhaustive `switch` over `ErrorKind` will need two new cases.

**Checks**
- **Before the change:** the new tests failed. The Python one reproduced the issue: `assert 'internal' == 'auth_required'`.
- **After the change:** Node tests pass (94 of 94), with clean typecheck, Biome format and oxlint. Python tests pass (83 of 83), with clean ruff format and ruff check.
- **Tests catch a regression:** with the Node `_meta` lookup removed, the three declared-kind tests fail.
- **CI:** hasn't reported yet.

**Cleanup:** the local worktree is removed. The commit (d46702e) is on the remote branch `worktree-explicit-error-kind`. Your staged changes on `main` weren't touched.

**Next step:** once this is released, `immigration-mcp` needs to set the `_meta` key on its sign-in, payment and "No current ... on file" results. Its REST path (`workers/mcp/src/rest.ts:352`) needs to set `error_kind` itself instead of calling `classifyError`.

result: Draft PR #83 lets MCP servers mark failed tool calls as `auth_required` or `payment_required` instead of `internal` (Node and Python, tests pass, CI pending).
